topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: I walked through the door of the restaurant, the air heavy with the scent of basil and the familiar hum of violins, only to find a note hanging where the waiter usually stands. "We are closing," it said, as if the walls themselves were whispering goodbyes. Each tile on the floor seemed to echo the words, and the chandelier above flickered, a soft, reluctant sadness. I wandered through the tables, my mind tracing the outlines of countless evenings, each dish a memory, each conversation a lingering taste. The closing wasn’t just of a place but of a chapter, a sweet, tender farewell to something that had become a part of me. I stood there, the world around me holding its breath, until the sun dipped below the horizon, painting everything in gold.
